name: Design System

hero.title: Write every variant once. Get every combination, dark mode included.
hero.lede: Describe states, sizes and variants as separate dimensions and rocketstyle turns each into a typed prop, with `mode(light, dark)` right next to the value. Underneath: the CSS-in-JS engine that beat Emotion and goober on every operation we timed, plus layout primitives, a responsive grid and motion.

why.title: The parts of a design system every team rebuilds.

items.title: Dimensions, not branches
items.text: `.states()`, `.sizes()` and `.variants()` each describe one axis. `<Button state="danger" size="lg">` merges base → state → size → variant at render. Five dimensions are built in, and a custom one (`tones` → `tone="warn"`) is one line of config.

items.title: Dark mode lives next to the value
items.text: Write `mode('#c2410c', '#ff5e1a')` inside `.theme()` or any dimension. `<PyreonUI mode="system">` follows the OS, and `init({ cssVariables: true })` turns a flip into one attribute write on `<html>`.

items.title: An engine that wins its benchmarks
items.text: styler beat Emotion by 3.4–6.3× and goober by 2.2–4.0× on cold insert, warm dedup, dynamic resolve and SSR collect; SSR collect also beat styled-components 2.3× (one run). Rules dedupe by hash, and the SSR `<style>` takes a CSP nonce.

items.title: One system for iOS and Android too
items.text: `styled(Prim)`, `Element`, coolgrid, attrs, `<PyreonUI>` and rocketstyle chains over a primitive lower to SwiftUI and Compose, with `defineTheme` tokens resolved at compile time. Experimental: a rocketstyle state flip is asserted on both device gates.

difference.title: Variants as data, not as ternaries.

before.label: React + styled-components
before.caption: Each dimension is a ternary inside every rule it touches, and dark mode nests another one inside that.

after.label: Pyreon + rocketstyle
after.caption: Each dimension is declared once and becomes a typed prop. Dark mode is `mode()` beside the value.

extraSectionsHtml:
inside the design system

Eleven packages, one system.

Use the whole thing through your components, or take only the layer you need: styler works on its own.

@pyreon/rocketstyledimensions

States, sizes, variants and your own axes as typed props.

@pyreon/stylerCSS-in-JS

styled, css, keyframes and global styles, deduplicated and SSR-safe.

@pyreon/unistyleresponsive engine

Breakpoints, responsive values and themes as CSS variables.

@pyreon/attrscomposition

Chainable default props; call-site props always win.

@pyreon/elementslayout

Element, Text, List, Overlay and Portal.

@pyreon/coolgridgrid

Container, Row and Col with your own columns and breakpoints.

@pyreon/ui-coreprovider

PyreonUI: theme and light, dark or system mode in one component.

@pyreon/kineticmotion

Enter, leave, collapse, stagger and keyed-list animation on CSS transitions. See Motion →

@pyreon/kinetic-presetsmotion

122 ready-made animations, imported one by one.

@pyreon/document-primitivesdocuments

18 document components (DocPage, DocTable, DocText…) themed like the rest of your UI.

@pyreon/connector-documentdocuments

The bridge from ui-system components to the @pyreon/document export pipeline.

features.title: Eleven packages that make one design system.

items.name: rocketstyle:
items.text: five built-in dimensions plus your own, each a typed prop, with results cached per definition

items.name: Server rendering:
items.text: per-request sheets, a CSP nonce on the critical `<style>`, and a streaming flush

items.name: elements:
items.text: Element, Text, List, Overlay and Portal layout primitives

items.name: useOverlay:
items.text: dropdowns, tooltips and modals with viewport flip, Escape, click-outside and a focus trap for modals

items.name: coolgrid:
items.text: Container, Row and Col; every numeric prop takes a value, a mobile-first array or a breakpoint object

items.name: PyreonUI:
items.text: one provider for theme and mode, plus `cssVariablesPrePaintScript()` so dark mode never flashes

items.name: attrs:
items.text: chainable default props on any component, and whatever the call site passes still wins

items.name: More of it on native:
items.text: several dynamic dimensions, nested style ternaries, pressed styles and `<List>` lower to iOS and Android

limits.title: You build the components
limits.text: These packages are the system, not a widget kit. A ready-made component library built on them exists in the repo but is not published yet, so today your Button is about twenty lines of rocketstyle.

limits.title: Give the grid its theme
limits.text: Container, Row and Col read columns and breakpoints from context. Render them under coolgrid's `Provider theme={theme}`, or a `PyreonUI` theme that carries the grid keys; without them a responsive Col is moved off-screen and a fixed size is ignored.

limits.title: CSS variables buy a clean flip, not speed
limits.text: `cssVariables` mode makes dark mode one attribute write with no flash. In our overnight run (300 components flipping 20 times, nine runs on a dev server), classic mode was 1.13× faster, so pick it for the flip, not the clock.

limits.title: Native lowers the authored patterns
limits.text: The CSS runtime stays on the web. Responsive values, `Overlay`, `Portal` and arbitrary selectors warn by name in a native build.

benchmarks.h: The fastest CSS-in-JS engine we measured, on all four operations.
benchmarks.p: styler is the engine under every rocketstyle component. Static styles resolve once; repeats hit a hash-keyed dedup cache, and SSR collection inserts each rule in constant time. styled-components appears only in SSR collect, where its figure includes a React render pass.

comingFrom.title: Keep your tagged templates.
comingFrom.note: Same template syntax, same `$`-transient props; the import changes. `styled.button` works too. For iOS and Android, wrap a primitive instead of an HTML tag: `styled(Prim)` is the form the native compiler lowers.

recipes.title: A theme toggle with one card definition
recipes.text: `PyreonUI` takes a signal-driven mode. The card declares both colours once; flipping the signal swaps its class, nothing remounts.

recipes.title: A responsive product grid
recipes.text: One column on phones, two from `sm`, three from `md`. Array values are mobile-first and cascade upward.
recipes.code:
import { For } from '@pyreon/core'
import { Provider, Container, Row, Col, theme } from '@pyreon/coolgrid'

const products = ['Zero', 'Native', 'Charts', 'Forms', 'Flow', 'Table']

export const ProductGrid = () => (
  <Provider theme={theme}>
    <Container gap={16}>
      <Row>
        <For each={products} by={(name) => name}>
          {(name) => <Col size={[12, 6, 4]}>{name}</Col>}
        </For>
      </Row>
    </Container>
  </Provider>
)

faq.q: Do I need all eleven packages?
faq.a: No. styler has no other ui-system dependency and works on its own. rocketstyle brings styler and ui-core; elements and coolgrid bring unistyle. kinetic and the document packages are separate installs.

faq.q: Does changing the theme or mode re-render my components?
faq.a: No. A theme or mode change re-resolves the CSS and updates the class name in place; components run once and nothing remounts.

Yes for markup: `class` is passed through as written, and kinetic takes Tailwind utilities through `.enterClass()` / `.leaveClass()`. The design system earns its place when you want themed, dimensioned components with dark mode built in.

faq.q: Does it work with SSR and streaming?
faq.a: Yes. `sheet.getStyleTag(nonce)` inlines the critical CSS for string rendering, `createSheet()` isolates a request, and a streaming flush sends only the rules each chunk needs.

In our overnight run, styler beat Emotion and goober on all four timed operations and styled-components on SSR collect. One run, author-run, synthetic; the reproduce command is `bun scripts/bench/core/styler.ts`.
